strings.name: Tim Berners-Lee
strings.role: Inventor of the Web · Open-standards advocate
strings.summary: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee proposed and implemented the World Wide Web, connecting hypertext through the internet. He established W3C to advance interoperable standards and advocated open access and personal-data control. The Web is an information system built on the internet, not the invention of the internet itself.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2025, not an exhaustive news record. Institutional achievements are team efforts; announced plans are not completed results.
strings.influence.rationale: Invented the Web and promoted open standards, connectivity, personal-data control and wider access.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Physics degree, The Queen’s College, Oxford, 1976
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Created the World Wide Web
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Designed the Web, wrote its first browser and server, and advanced HTTP, HTML and URIs.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Standards and data agency
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Promoted interoperability and personal control of data through W3C and projects including Solid.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Published a memoir
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Released This Is For Everyone, reflecting on the Web’s origins and future.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Promoted Solid and Inrupt
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Publicly advanced Solid and Inrupt as ways to improve personal control of data.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Received the 2016 ACM Turing Award for the Web and its foundational technologies.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Web Foundation established
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Co-founded the organization to promote access and the public interest.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Founded W3C
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Established the Web standards consortium at MIT.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Web software freely released
strings.timeline.event-6.text: CERN placed Web software in the public domain, encouraging open adoption.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First browser and server
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Implemented early Web software and foundational protocols at CERN.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Proposed the Web
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Proposed a hypertext system linking scientific information.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Graduated from Oxford
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Earned a physics degree at The Queen’s College.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in London
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in a family involved in early computing.
